participants.note: Approach ACK; argued that failing hard with CORRUPT is correct, contributed a unit test, and opened doc PR #35944 for wallet recovery guidance
objected that failing to load locks users without backups out of uncorrupted funds; also caught an invalid unit test
Concept ACK; suggested adding a release note
Concept ACK; supports failing fast on load rather than automatically attempting unreliable repairs
Approach ACK, but reported that stored and calculated hashes are inverted in the corruption error message
concerned that returning early on mismatch locks users out of their wallet and funds rather than allowing recovery

claims.text: users with corrupted wallets who lack backups cannot access uncorrupted funds or export descriptors
claims.quote: If we disable allowing this corrupted wallets, users that unconsciously did not create a backup will be unable to access any of their funds at all without switching to an old Core version.

claims.text: the unit test passes due to an EOF deserialization failure rather than exercising the hash mismatch corruption code path
claims.quote: This test is wrong it is not testing the `DBErrors::CORRUPT` path intended to test.

claims.text: the error message inverts stored and actual hashes, causing users inspecting the database manually to look for the wrong key
claims.quote: The two are swapped. In the description you call the DB key the stored hash and `wtx.GetHash()` the calculated one, and here the `strprintf` passes them the other way round.

claims.text: early return on mismatch locks users out of their wallet and funds instead of allowing them to export wallet data or access remaining funds
claims.quote: This early return means locking the user out of their wallet and their funds, wallet-load rescan on the other hand somehow sucks.

support.reason: When a tx record's stored hash doesn't match the hash of its deserialized content, returning NEED_RESCAN was the wrong response: the rescan is not a reliable repair... failing hard with CORRUPT makes sense
Concept ACK. Worth a release note?
I do prefer the wallet to stop and fail fast instead of trying to fix rare corrupted scenarios automatically _everytime on load_, which makes the wallet do too much and bloats the codebase as well.
Built it, ran the unit tests and the wallet functional tests, and reproduced the corruption on regtest.

waiting_on.what: fix inverted stored and calculated hashes in the error message
address vicjuma's concern regarding locking users out of wallet funds

result.notes: Added vicjuma as a participant with an objection regarding locking users out of their wallets upon record mismatch, which remains open along with jeanpablojp's comment on inverted hashes.
